summary_paragraph: Mr. ___ was admitted with nausea, vomiting, and dehydration in the setting of multiple myeloma and immunocompromise. He had not taken his Revlimid recently and presented with symptoms suggestive of a gastrointestinal infection, possibly viral or bacterial, with reactive joint pain. Workup included negative CT head and chest X-ray, and CT abdomen showed persistent but improved colonic thickening, likely from resolving diverticulitis or colitis. Stool studies were negative for pathogens. He was treated with IV fluids, Ciprofloxacin, and Metronidazole for presumed gastroenteritis. His supratherapeutic INR of 3.3 led to a temporary hold on warfarin, with resumption at 5 mg nightly; ultrasound confirmed a non-occlusive DVT in the right femoral and popliteal veins. He improved clinically, remained afebrile, and was discharged home on oral antibiotics, adjusted warfarin, and home medications with instructions to follow up with his PCP and oncologist.
